whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the CPQ and Billing Accredited Professional exam?

personas.label: CPQ consultants expanding into Billing
personas.description: You already configure Salesforce CPQ and want to show that you can extend a solution through invoices, payments, and revenue schedules.

personas.label: Finance and operations teams
personas.description: You support recurring invoices, subscription charges, or revenue tracking in Salesforce and want to validate your quote-to-cash knowledge.

personas.label: Quote-to-cash implementation partners
personas.description: You design solutions that connect CPQ configuration with Salesforce Billing and want to demonstrate end-to-end implementation skills.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the CPQ and Billing AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This retired Accredited Professional exam covered CPQ and Billing implementation. The official Summer ’24 guide listed 35 scored questions, up to five unscored questions, 60 minutes, a 74% passing score, and a $150 fee.
bullets: 35 scored questions in 60 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions.
74% passing score in the official Summer ’24 exam guide.
Retired credential: Salesforce closed registration on July 24, 2026; the final exam date was August 31, 2026, and retirement is February 1, 2027.
Two product areas: review CPQ and Billing implementation, design, and quote-to-cash concepts.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice tracing a transaction through a CPQ and Billing org: configure a quote, create an order, generate an invoice, and review a revenue schedule. Aim for at least 75% on practice questions and be able to explain each record in the flow.

examFormat.heading: CPQ and Billing AP exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in person. It tests setup and process decisions across CPQ and Billing.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions may follow a sale from quote configuration through invoicing and revenue recognition. They can also describe a billing need, such as when to invoice a subscription or how to rate usage, and ask which setting supports it.
bestWayToPass: Follow the records: Learn how quote lines become order products and how Billing uses them to create invoices and invoice lines.
Review billing timing: Understand when charges are billed, billing frequency, and invoice consolidation.
Study usage charges: Know how usage summaries and rate cards help calculate consumption-based charges.
Understand revenue schedules: Review how revenue is distributed across accounting periods and how ratable and event-based recognition differ.

certificationCard.description: Historical CPQ and Billing Accredited Professional exam. The official Summer ’24 guide lists 35 scored questions plus up to five unscored questions, a 60-minute limit, 74% passing score, and $150 fee. The exam outline weights Revenue Cloud Technical Design (68%), Revenue Cloud Implementation Management (29%), and New Release Capabilities (3%).

keyConcepts.h2: CPQ and Billing AP: core concepts

blocks.heading: Quote-to-Cash Setup
blocks.body: Salesforce Billing extends a CPQ process into billing and payment activities. A quote can be ordered, producing order records that Billing uses to generate invoices. Billing policies can define invoice timing, payment terms, and consolidation behavior. Legal entities represent the billing entity involved in a transaction. Tax integrations can calculate tax on invoices. Be prepared to explain the record relationships and the setup needed for the process.

blocks.heading: Invoice Generation and Billing Rules
blocks.body: Billing rules define when and how a charge should be invoiced. Bill Now can invoice immediately; Bill in Advance invoices at the beginning of a period; Bill in Arrears invoices after a period ends. Billing frequency can be monthly, quarterly, annual, or one-time, depending on the product setup. An invoice run processes eligible charges and creates invoices with invoice lines. Credit notes can record adjustments, while billing batches can support high-volume processing.

blocks.heading: Usage-Based Billing
blocks.body: Usage billing supports variable charges based on consumption, such as API calls or data transfer. Usage records can be summarized for a billing period and rated using configured rates or tiers. The resulting rated usage can be included in invoicing. An overage charge applies when consumption exceeds an amount included in a subscription. Understand how usage data enters the process and how it becomes a billable charge.

blocks.heading: Payments and Failed Charges
blocks.body: Payment configuration connects invoices to payment methods and processors. Payment terms describe when an invoice is due. Auto-pay can charge a stored payment method according to the configured process. Dunning manages follow-up for failed payments, such as retry attempts and customer notices. Payment allocations connect payments to invoices, while refunds and credit memos can reverse or adjust charges. Know how these records support collections and account servicing.

blocks.heading: Revenue Recognition and Reporting
blocks.body: Revenue schedules spread revenue across periods when recognition follows a service term, or recognize it at a point in time when appropriate. Revenue recognition rules define the timing, and transactions record amounts for accounting periods. Finance period settings establish those period boundaries. Reports can help finance teams compare recognized and deferred revenue. Learn how changes to a contract can affect the schedule and its reporting.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the CPQ and Billing AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Trace each scenario across the quote-to-cash process. Identify whether it concerns quote setup, order creation, invoice timing, payments, or revenue recognition, then choose the feature that handles that step.

blocks.heading: Trace the Record Flow
blocks.body: Review how quote lines and orders connect to order products, subscriptions, invoice lines, and invoices. Know what action or process creates each record.

blocks.heading: Match Billing Timing to the Need
blocks.body: Distinguish immediate billing from advance and arrears billing. Also check the configured frequency and any consolidation requirements.

blocks.heading: Follow an Invoice Run
blocks.body: An invoice run processes eligible charges based on their billing schedule. Review the conditions that make a charge eligible and how invoice lines represent the individual charges.

blocks.heading: Understand Subscription Changes
blocks.body: Changes during a subscription term can affect charges for the remaining period. Review how amendments, quantity changes, and cancellations affect billing and proration.

blocks.heading: Review Revenue Timing
blocks.body: Revenue schedules allocate amounts to accounting periods according to the recognition rule. Check how the schedule should respond when the contract terms change.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after CPQ and Billing AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on quote-to-cash knowledge with a platform or customer-facing Salesforce credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A contracted sale should produce monthly invoices. Which CPQ Billing record supports the planned invoice dates?
options: A separate opportunity for each monthly charge
A billing schedule associated with the order product
A renewal contract for every monthly period
A new quote created at the start of each month
sampleQuestions.explanation: A billing schedule defines when eligible charges are due for invoicing across the subscription term.
whyWrong: Opportunities track sales work and are not created for each recurring invoice.
A billing schedule associated with the order product supports recurring invoice timing.
Renewal contracts cover later terms, not each billing period in the current term.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an invoice differ from an invoice line?
options: An invoice is only for subscriptions; a line is only for one-time items
The invoice stores tax and each line stores the payment
The invoice is the document, and its lines list the individual charges
The invoice is a draft while its lines are final posted records
sampleQuestions.explanation: The invoice is the overall billing record, while invoice lines represent the charges included on it.
whyWrong: Both subscriptions and one-time charges can appear on invoices depending on configuration.
Tax and payments are not divided between invoice and line in this way.
Invoice lines are part of the invoice rather than independently final records.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer upgrades during a contract and should pay only for the remaining term. What supports the adjusted charge?
options: Proration on the amendment
A replacement contract starting at the original date
A manual finance adjustment on a future invoice
A credit note for the full original annual amount
sampleQuestions.explanation: Proration on an amendment adjusts the charge to account for the remaining contract period.
whyWrong: A replacement contract is not needed to adjust a mid-term change.
A manual adjustment bypasses the amendment and proration process.
Crediting the full annual amount would not reflect the value of the upgrade.

sampleQuestions.question: What does revenue recognition determine?
options: The maximum discount permitted on a quote line
Which payment method a customer may use
When revenue is recorded relative to invoicing
Which currency is shown on an invoice
sampleQuestions.explanation: Revenue recognition determines when billed amounts are recognized as revenue for accounting purposes.
whyWrong: Discount limits affect quote pricing, not the timing of revenue recognition.
Payment methods control collection, not when revenue is recognized.
Invoice currency is separate from revenue timing.

sampleQuestions.question: A posted invoice contains an error. What is the appropriate way to correct the billed amount?
options: Edit the posted invoice and save it again
Issue a credit note against the invoice
Leave it unchanged and add a note to the account
Delete it and create a replacement invoice
sampleQuestions.explanation: A credit note records an adjustment against the posted invoice while preserving the billing history.
whyWrong: Posted invoices should not simply be edited to erase the original transaction.
An account note does not correct the invoiced amount or record the adjustment.
Deleting the posted invoice would remove the audit trail rather than make a traceable correction.

sampleQuestions.question: What action typically triggers order creation in a CPQ and Billing flow?
options: Saving a draft quote in the Quote Line Editor
Ordering the accepted quote
Adding the first subscription product to the quote
Submitting the quote for manager approval
sampleQuestions.explanation: Ordering the accepted quote creates the order that can continue into Billing.
whyWrong: A draft save preserves quote work but does not create the ordered transaction.
Adding a product configures the quote but does not order it.
Approval is a review step and is not itself the order trigger.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer pays only part of an invoice balance. How should the payment be recorded?
options: As a contract amendment lowering the term value
As a new invoice for the unpaid amount
As a partial payment allocated to the invoice
As a credit note for the unpaid balance
sampleQuestions.explanation: A partial payment is allocated against the invoice, leaving the remaining balance open.
whyWrong: An amendment changes contract terms rather than recording money received.
A second invoice would duplicate the charge instead of recording partial settlement.
A credit note reduces a charge; it does not represent a partial payment.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Billing rule control?
options: Which products a salesperson may add to a quote
Which approval chain a discounted quote follows
The order of quote lines in the editor
How and when charges are invoiced
sampleQuestions.explanation: Billing rules define the timing and method used to invoice charges.
whyWrong: Product availability is controlled through product setup and rules.
Approval routing is managed by approval configuration.
Quote line display order is separate from billing rules.

sampleQuestions.question: A January-to-December subscription is billed quarterly. How many billing periods are there?
options: Twelve monthly periods
One period for the entire contract
Four quarterly periods
Three periods because the first is billed with the order
sampleQuestions.explanation: A one-year term billed quarterly has four billing periods.
whyWrong: Monthly billing would produce twelve periods, but this subscription is quarterly.
A single period would represent one-time or annual billing, not quarterly billing.
The order does not remove a quarter from the billing schedule.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a tax rule do in CPQ Billing?
options: Determines how tax is calculated for a charge
Blocks invoice posting until a tax reference is entered
Reports annual tax collected by a legal entity
Converts tax to the company functional currency
sampleQuestions.explanation: A tax rule determines how tax should be calculated for the charge under the configured tax setup.
whyWrong: A tax rule calculates tax; it does not necessarily impose that particular posting condition.
Reporting summarizes tax after calculation and does not define the calculation itself.
Currency conversion is a separate finance or tax integration behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use an evergreen subscription instead of a fixed-term subscription?
options: The purchase has no recurring service component
The service continues until it is canceled
The contract must be renegotiated at every term end
The customer wants annual rather than monthly invoices
sampleQuestions.explanation: An evergreen subscription continues until a cancellation ends it rather than expiring on a fixed end date.
whyWrong: Evergreen describes a recurring service, not a one-time purchase.
It does not require renewal negotiations at a fixed term boundary.
Invoice frequency is independent of whether a subscription is evergreen.

sampleQuestions.question: An order is active but no invoice has been generated. What is a likely reason?
options: The next billing date has not arrived yet
The quote was not approved before ordering
The customer is missing an industry value
The product is configured as a bundle
sampleQuestions.explanation: If billing follows a schedule, no invoice may be due until the next scheduled billing date.
whyWrong: The order being active indicates it has already passed the relevant order process.
An industry value is not generally required to determine billing schedule timing.
Bundled products can still be billed according to their setup.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an invoice run do?
options: Reprices open quotes with current price book values
Closes the accounting period to further postings
Resends every unpaid invoice by email
Creates invoices from charges whose schedules are due
sampleQuestions.explanation: An invoice run processes due billable charges and generates their invoices.
whyWrong: Quote repricing is separate from invoice generation.
Closing an accounting period is a finance-period control, not an invoice run.
An invoice run generates invoices rather than simply resending existing ones.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer cancels a prepaid annual subscription halfway through the term. What may be issued for the unused period?
options: A renewal quote starting on the cancellation date
An amendment that increases the contract value
A new invoice for months of service not delivered
A credit for the unused portion of the term
sampleQuestions.explanation: A credit can account for the unused prepaid service when the subscription is canceled, subject to the configured policy.
whyWrong: A renewal starts a later term and does not handle unused prepaid value.
Cancellation does not normally increase the contract value for undelivered service.
Billing the customer for undelivered months would not provide the described adjustment.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement describes the relationship between CPQ and Billing?
options: CPQ creates the order, and Billing invoices the ordered charges
Billing creates the quote, and CPQ collects customer payments
They are alternatives, so an org can use only one
CPQ manages subscriptions while Billing handles only one-time charges
sampleQuestions.explanation: CPQ supports product configuration and quoting through order creation; Billing processes the charges for invoicing.
whyWrong: Billing does not replace CPQ for quote creation, and payment collection is not CPQ’s role.
CPQ and Billing can work together as parts of a quote-to-cash process.
Billing can support recurring subscription charges as well as other configured charges.
